change: Yield to the browser event loop between cached replanned WebAssembly atomic actions, without changing the search or game rules.
site_deployment: Owner-private Site v64 unchanged; both versions served locally.

environment.browser: Zen 1.22.3b with the same isolated profile for both runs
environment.display: 1440x900 private Xvfb desktop with a visible browser window
environment.server: Local development server, baseline and candidate run serially
environment.wasm_artifacts: Baseline and candidate WebAssembly SHA-256 identical
environment.probe: Capture end-turn click timestamps, requestAnimationFrame timestamps, painted turn/status text, and final viewport pixels

scenario.human_actions: End turn only; no purchases or moves

human_seat_0.outcome: Both runs reached the same nonterminal turn-11 human position.

human_seat_1.measurement_window: Turns 6 through 10, after identical unmeasured turn-1-through-5 setup
human_seat_1.outcome: Both runs reached the same turn-11 cyan terminal win after 96 actions.

interpretation: The synchronous baseline did not paint BOT THINKING on any measured reply; its first post-click paint was the completed turn.
The candidate painted BOT THINKING on every measured reply, with maximum click-to-first-paint 136 ms across these two fixed-seat windows.
The candidate did not reduce total reply latency: its complete replies were generally slower, especially the seat-0 turn-10 reply (2207 versus 1367 ms).
Exact viewport pixel agreement at the end of each deterministic seat run supports visible outcome parity, but does not prove complete hidden-state or per-action parity.
limitations: One inspected symmetric map and one browser/profile, with no predeclared responsiveness threshold or procedural-map distribution.
RequestAnimationFrame timing and painted DOM text are browser observations, not a device-representative input-latency guarantee.
The seat-1 first monitor expired before the first five clicks, so only turns 6-10 have paired frame measurements.
The seat-0 maximum frame gaps include the blocked click-to-first-frame interval; seat-1 maximum subsequent gaps exclude that interval, which is separately reported as click-to-first-paint.
This is a local development server, not the deployed owner-private Site or its in-app browser.
decision: Keep the cooperative scheduler on the experimental branch and leave Site v64 unchanged pending a predeclared procedural-map, both-seat browser responsiveness and complete-action parity gate.
